qs.q: A 55-year-old patient presents with acute pain, swelling, and local tenderness over the supraspinatus tendon, with overlying skin that is hot and red. Plain radiographs show tendon calcification. What is the most likely diagnosis?
qs.e: Acute calcific periarthritis typically occurs particularly in the supraspinatus tendon, presenting with acute pain, swelling, and local tenderness with tendon calcification on X-rays. Chondrocalcinosis refers to the asymptomatic or imaging-based presence of cartilage calcification rather than acute tendon inflammation.

qs.q: A 68-year-old woman presents with severe pain, swelling, and local tenderness developing rapidly around her right shoulder, with the overlying skin becoming hot and red. Plain radiographs reveal tendon calcification, particularly in the supraspinatus tendon. What is the primary underlying cause of this presentation?
qs.e: Acute calcific periarthritis is caused by basic calcium phosphate (BCP) deposition, particularly in the supraspinatus tendon, leading to rapid pain and swelling mimicking infection. CPPD typically affects the joint rather than presenting primarily as acute calcific periarthritis of a tendon.
